svg.title: Fortified UK flour adds about 100 micrograms of folic acid a day
svg.desc: Average extra folic acid eaten per day from non-wholemeal wheat flour fortified at 250 micrograms per 100 grams, after a 25% processing loss and 11.3% imported flour: everyone 98, women 19 to 34 93, women 35 to 49 80, adults 65 and over 88, men 19 to 34 130, boys 14 to 18 136 micrograms. The pregnancy supplement is 400 micrograms and the adult upper level is 1,000 micrograms.

text.font-family: Inter, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: 250 µg is the amount in 100 g of flour, not a daily dose. To get 1,000 µg from flour alone, an adult would

svg.text: need about 600 g of fortified flour a day, about 10 times the UK average of 59 g. People already average

text.font-family: Inter, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: 79 µg a day from fortified cereals, spreads and supplements; modelling puts the total at 176 µg after fortification.
